ranked.headline: Perturbation and drug response models are judged on generalizability and transport
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications benchmark perturbation response models on transportability, generalizability, and performance against baseline profiles.

ranked.headline: Single-cell data are resolving regulatory and risk effects to specific cell types
ranked.summary: Single-cell atlases, communication methods and deep learning models now assign regulatory and drug effects to individual cell states.

ranked.headline: Statistical frameworks for technical variation in single-cell and multi-omic integration
ranked.summary: Growing multiplexed, long-read, spatial, and multi-omic datasets demand explicit handling of batch, replicate, and imputation effects.

ranked.headline: Molecular ML models scored on named endpoints and experimental selection steps
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications tie learned molecular models to explicit toxicity, ADMET, binding, and active-learning endpoints rather than training…

ranked.headline: Single-cell and spatial profiling links regulatory layers across chromatin and RNA
ranked.summary: Single-cell and spatial methods now resolve methylation, chromatin contacts and RNA interactions at cell-type resolution in tissues and differentiation.

ranked.headline: Explicit interaction structure in PDE and reduced models of spreading and signaling
ranked.summary: Preprints from December 2025 pair explicit interaction structure with reduction or spatial coupling across epidemic, signaling, and microbial systems.

ranked.headline: Comparative genomics links gene content, selection and repeats to ecology and evolution
ranked.summary: Large-scale genome surveys now attribute gene content, selective sweeps and repeat landscapes to specific evolutionary and ecological drivers.

ranked.headline: Glycoproteins Drive Antibody Escape and Structural Adaptation Across Viruses
ranked.summary: Recent studies probe glycan-dependent antibody recognition, JN.1-lineage immune evasion, and H3 hemagglutinin drift amid zoonotic and variant concerns.

ranked.headline: Integrating antigen quality, HLA context and population risk to rank neoantigens
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a glioma study score neoantigens and pHLA off-targets using joint quality, HLA and population-aware features.

ranked.headline: Pathology foundation models gain multi-omics alignment and fairness-aware adaptation
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications extend pathology foundation models to omics alignment, spatial omics generation, and cross-cohort fairness.

ranked.headline: Genome-resolved comparisons are redefining microbial and algal lineage boundaries
ranked.summary: Genome-scale comparisons now resolve ecotypes, convergent traits, and deep algal branches across bacterial and eukaryotic lineages.

ranked.headline: Scale-aware models reconcile heterogeneous spatial and temporal scales in neural data
ranked.summary: Week-long clinical intracranial recordings and paired spike-LFP data now support pretrained and multiscale models of neural activity.

ranked.headline: Spatial and lineage models infer single-cell fate and 3D genome organization
ranked.summary: Single-cell lineage, spatial, and chromatin tracing datasets now demand explicit models of error, geometry, and developmental mode.

ranked.headline: Single-cell methods address scale, trajectory, and cell-type structure in RNA data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published method target scale, uncertainty, and biological context in scRNA-seq analysis.

ranked.headline: Multi-omics fusion and graph embeddings advance drug response prediction models
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs attention-based multi-omics fusion with protein network embeddings to predict BRAF inhibitor sensitivity in cell lines.

ranked.headline: Imputation and cross-platform calibration reduce array-specific bias in omics data
ranked.summary: Multi-array and biobank-scale studies combine platforms, so platform-specific bias in clocks, methylation, and genotypes requires explicit correction.

ranked.headline: Simulation and prediction methods probed at the limits of their reliable accuracy
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers test where structure prediction and simulation methods stay accurate, from disordered-protein design to membrane protein affinity.

ranked.headline: Machine learning and benchmarks assess RNA modification and siRNA prediction tools
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a published study evaluate computational tools for RNA modification detection, extracellular vesicle RNA sorting, and siRNA efficacy.

ranked.headline: Multiscale simulations map RNA, glycan, and chemokine-receptor binding at atomic detail
ranked.summary: Coarse-grained and all-atom simulations now resolve binding interfaces and conformational restriction across RNA-protein, receptor, and glycan systems.

ranked.headline: Curated genomic references and new comparison tools across bacteria, fungi and viruses
ranked.summary: Standardized reference collections and audited assemblies are becoming the basis for reproducible comparative genomics across microbial and viral taxa.

ranked.headline: Learned alignment and integration of spatial and single-cell multiomics
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and published methods apply contrastive, graph, and optimal transport models to align and integrate spatial and single-cell multiomics data.

ranked.headline: Sparse E/I connectivity and biological constraints shape the range of neural dynamics
ranked.summary: Three December 2025 studies connect E/I balance and sparse connectivity to constraints on spectra, trained network dynamics, and human brain synchrony.

ranked.headline: Context-Conditioned Models of Amino Acid Identity Across Design and Immunology
ranked.summary: Structure-conditioned diffusion, context-dependent mutation inference, and MHC representation benchmarks all address sequence context in residue prediction.

ranked.headline: Genome-scale metabolic models link microbial metabolism to host phenotypes and growth
ranked.summary: Population-scale genome sets and multi-omic context now let genome-scale models address strain-level metabolic heterogeneity and host associations.

ranked.headline: Biophysical models link axon geometry and myelin damage to conduction behavior
ranked.summary: Anatomically resolved simulations now yield quantitative functional readouts for axons, peripheral nerves, and brain stimulation.

ranked.headline: Open-source tools encode recurring omics operations into standards and interfaces
ranked.summary: Recent open-source releases package recurring proteomics, genomics, and LC-MS analysis steps into reusable standards, interfaces, and benchmarks.

ranked.headline: Stochastic fluctuations are being used to infer mechanism in molecular systems
ranked.summary: Simulation and theory now separate noise sources in smFRET, gene switches, and expression networks, treating fluctuations as mechanistic information.

ranked.headline: Sequence-resolved repeat-rich chromosome regions across populations and pedigrees
ranked.summary: Long-read and T2T assemblies now resolve centromeres, telomeres and rDNA at population and multigenerational scale.

ranked.headline: Integrating multi-omics and genetic data to test non-additive and network-level effects
ranked.summary: Cross-platform replication and public multi-omics resources are now used to test non-additive genetic and network-level associations.

ranked.headline: Chromosome-scale genomes reveal architecture and size evolution across three lineages
ranked.summary: Recent chromosome-scale assemblies of flatworm, lamprey and Physaria genomes enable direct comparison of structural and size evolution.

ranked.headline: Variant calling and classification shape mutational signature and germline inference
ranked.summary: Consensus calling, interpretable tabular models and open rule automation are being benchmarked as reusable pipelines for variant-level inference.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks of structure predictors and docking for binding affinity prediction
ranked.summary: Deep-learning co-folding models are now benchmarked against docking and affinity data for ligands, nanobodies, and protein partners.

ranked.headline: Benchmarking antimicrobial resistance prediction from genomes and sequencing reads
ranked.summary: Studies now expose sampling-confounded ML resistance prediction and RGI bit-score errors, as nanopore workflows target bloodstream infections.

ranked.headline: Learned surrogates pair neural representations with dynamical and planning objectives
ranked.summary: Neural models now serve as fast surrogates for chemical reaction networks, gene regulatory dynamics, and cell-fate planning in recent preprints.

ranked.headline: Computational design of binders, peptides and PROTACs guided by structural models
ranked.summary: Recent preprints couple generative models and structure-based design across PROTACs, peptides, and protein binders.

ranked.headline: Splicing variation and NMD efficiency profiled across tumors, glia, and normal tissue
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers quantify NMD efficiency, retrotransposon activity, and exon-level splicing variation from transcriptome and long-read sequencing…

ranked.headline: Computational tracking of atoms, stereochemistry, and biosynthetic product structure
ranked.summary: Recent preprints apply structure-aware computation to atom provenance, stereochemical metabolite assignment, and biosynthetic product classification.

ranked.headline: Graph and synteny algorithms compact sequence elements and align chains to pangenome paths
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend path enumeration, gene-tree to pedigree linkage, and breakpoint-free synteny block derivation with explicit algorithmic formulations.

ranked.headline: Learned models increasingly drive identification from mass spectrometry data
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs de novo and model-based inference with new acquisition and database strategies across peptides, glycans, and natural products.

ranked.headline: Computational tools for isoform switching, regulatory modules, and sequencing cohort QC
ranked.summary: Long-read, single-cell, and large cohort sequencing datasets require analysis tools that yield quantitative, comparable outputs.
